currentContext.strengths: Deep last-mile physical distribution: the agent network had grown to over 1.7 million agents across 2.6 lakh villages and 6,475 blocks as of March 2026, a footprint that is hard to replicate for assisted rural financial services.|Trusted, daily touchpoints that give a structural advantage in serving rural customers whose service, trust and assistance needs differ materially from urban markets.|Proprietary transaction data on agents' cash flows and behaviour, used to develop customised credit products and to convert field-level data into MSME credit signals.|Distribution operating leverage: gross margin grew ~13% in FY26 while indirect costs did not grow, and EBIT expanded 2.4x, indicating fee-product rollout rides on an already-built cost base.|Debt-free balance sheet - the MD&A states the Company is debt-free, with only cash credit facilities taken to manage treasury funds.|Cross-sell traction: 23% of active Adhikaris now offer two or more financial products beyond basic cash withdrawal, evidencing the network can carry higher-margin categories.|365-day, seven-language customer support integrated with the partner web and mobile applications, supporting an agent base that needs assisted service.
currentContext.strategies: Mission framed as using technology to transform how Bharat banks, executed through three building blocks: expanding the network of Assisted Digital Touchpoint Operators (Spice Money Adhikaris) as a cost-efficient alternative to ATMs and bank branches; empowering that network to deliver a full suite of own and partner financial products; and creating digital products and apps for new-to-tech, under-banked consumers.|Shift the growth thesis from adding touchpoints to deepening each touchpoint: management states the marginal contribution to business value from further network expansion will be lower than in the past, so the next phase focuses on the depth and value of the financial relationships each touchpoint can support.|Expand the monthly active and high-throughput Adhikari cohorts and raise transaction volume and value per outlet, converting a single-purpose cash-out network into a multi-product financial services hub - in management's words, turning the metaphorical ATM network into a full-fledged Financial Services Branch Network.|Retain and defend the AePS anchor while accelerating the rollout of high-margin fee products across the active base rather than relying solely on network expansion.|Innovate within the AePS ecosystem, with AePS-Cash Deposit (digitising small-value cash deposits for banks through Adhikari outlets) positioned as an emerging growth engine.|Scale UPI Cash Point - cash withdrawal at an Adhikari point using any UPI app - as the template for moving from isolated cash events to long-term, comprehensive financial relationships.|Deepen the banking relationship beyond transactions by distributing partner products - CASA, loans, credit cards and insurance - to increase customer lifetime value across rural India.|Embed AI and automation across business, engineering and operations to raise productivity, cut costs and generate MSME credit signals from field-level data.|Maintain cost discipline: gross margin growth without growth in indirect costs is the stated route to operating leverage.
currentContext.expansion: This is an asset-light, service business: the annual report discloses no plants, no manufacturing capacity and no rupee capex programme. 'Expansion' is expressed as network footprint and new product engines. The agent network had grown to over 1.7 million agents across 2.6 lakh villages and 6,475 blocks as of March 2026, and management states that the marginal contribution to business value from further network expansion is now lower than in the past, so the next phase of expansion is depth per touchpoint rather than more touchpoints - expanding the monthly active and high-throughput Adhikari cohorts and raising transaction volume and value per outlet. New engines are being funded from operations: EBIT for FY26 was struck after Rs 9 crore of investment in Spice UPI and Credit, described as spend for driving future expansion. Product-level expansion in FY26 covered UPI Cash Point (annualised GTV run-rate of Rs. 3,500 cr), AePS-Cash Deposit (GTV up 1.8x to Rs. 1,560 cr after 2.8x growth in FY25, with more leading banks expected to adopt it) and continued rollout of high-margin fee products across the active base. Structural expansion also runs through corporate actions: a Scheme of Amalgamation merging Spice Money Limited, E-Arth Travel Solutions Private Limited and Vikasni Fintech Private Limited into DiGiSPICE is in progress (BSE and NSE NOCs in September 2025, first motion petition filed with NCLT on March 7, 2026, shareholders meeting held July 13, 2026, second motion application filed July 24, 2026), and the Company acquired 8,69,030 Class B shares (100% of Class B shares) in Spice Money Limited from Sood Informatics LLP. In the other direction, step-down subsidiary Spice Digital FZCO (Dubai) was wound up and dissolved with effect from April 18, 2025.

risks.note: The Spice Money business operates under licences from RBI, UIDAI, IRCTC and banks as part of banking correspondence arrangements; changes to existing regulations, new compliance requirements or modifications in KYC norms and interchange fees could impact operations. Interchange economics sit outside the Company's control, so a regulatory change can reset unit economics for the whole network.

The business relies heavily on a technology platform that agents use remotely to execute large numbers of financial transactions, exposing it to IT and financial risks common to banking systems plus software and network issues such as data security breaches, unauthorised data access and firewall vulnerabilities. An outage or breach halts transaction revenue at every touchpoint simultaneously.

The high volume of financial transactions is susceptible to cyber fraud; the Company relies on insurance, KYC norms and standardised processes as safeguards, and states that data science and machine learning have significantly reduced fraud risk. Losses in an assisted, agent-operated model are borne centrally even when the failure is at the last mile.

The entry of new, well-capitalised players into the fintech sector is driving up acquisition costs and squeezing profit margins - a structural margin risk for a business whose growth thesis now rests on higher-margin fee products.

Collaborations with banks as Banking Correspondent (BC) partners involve non-real-time settlement processes, exposing the business to risks associated with bank sustainability and to disruption of operations. The Company carries settlement exposure to partner banks it does not control.

risks.risk: Concentration on AePS as the primary margin engine
risks.note: AePS remains the primary margin contributor, generating 59% of total gross margin, while the off-us AePS industry faces growth headwinds as banks increasingly prioritise on-us transactions. Growth depends on new fee products replacing a maturing anchor category.

Of 16.6 lac Adhikaris, the monthly active base is close to 4 lac, and roughly 80,000 high-throughput Adhikaris contribute 85% of total Gross Transaction Value - a small cohort carries most of the throughput, so attrition or competitive poaching within it has disproportionate impact.

risks.risk: Dependence on a single material subsidiary
risks.note: Substantially all operations run through material subsidiary Spice Money Limited, which engages in AePS and m-ATM, cash deposit, cash collection, account opening, lending, PPI, wallet-based UPI and bill payment services; the listed entity's earnings therefore track one operating company and one regulatory perimeter.

one-line thesis: DiGiSPICE has transformed from an AEPS-focused agent network into a multi-product financial inclusion platform, with UPI Cash Point and agent lending now driving margin expansion and profitability, while regulatory tailwinds around BC banking outlets create a multi-year growth runway.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Through its material subsidiary Spice Money Limited, the Company provides financial technology services - AePS and m-ATM cash withdrawal, cash deposit, cash collection, account opening, lending services, prepaid instruments (PPI), a wallet-based UPI app and bill payment services - delivered by a network of local agents called Spice Money Adhikaris. The Adhikari acts as an assisted, trusted last-mile touchpoint for consumers and micro-enterprises in villages and small towns who are cash-first and need help with product understanding, KYC, onboarding and issue resolution. The stated direction is to move each touchpoint from single-purpose cash withdrawal to a multi-product hub distributing partner banking, savings, protection and credit products alongside the Company's own credit offering.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- AePS remains the primary margin contributor at 59% of total gross margin, but the off-us AePS industry faces growth headwinds as banks increasingly prioritise on-us transactions, and as the category reaches structural maturity its contribution to incremental growth will naturally moderate.
- Market-share gain within a headwind category: off-us AePS share rose from 17.3% to 18.4%, with AePS GTV of Rs. 59,405 cr versus Rs. 51,221 cr in FY25 and AePS gross margin of Rs. 110 cr versus Rs. 97 cr.
- AePS-Cash Deposit is expected to become a significant driver of transaction volumes as more leading banks adopt the service; its GTV grew 1.8x this year to Rs. 1,560 cr after growing 2.8x in FY25.
- Collections is the first vertical where the relationship has been deepened, contributing approximately 41% of total GTV and approximately 19.6% of gross margin.
- Gross margin expanded from Rs. 178 crore to Rs. 201.2 crore (~13%) while indirect costs did not grow, lifting EBIT 2.4x - operating leverage on an already-built network is the stated margin lever.
- EBIT was struck after investment in the new engines (Spice UPI and Credit), which management frames as spend for future expansion rather than run-rate cost.
- The Credit business is nearing break-even on current operating trends and is expected to turn profitable in the near term.
- Treasury income is directly linked to balances maintained for operations, so management points to EBIT rather than EBITDA as the relevant performance indicator.
- Demand narrative: Spice Money is positioned to capitalise on India's rural digital revolution using its Adhikari network and diversified portfolio, while navigating regulatory and competitive challenges.
- Competitive pressure is an explicit headwind - entry of new, well-capitalised fintech players is driving up acquisition costs and squeezing profit margins.

margins.body: Gross margin expanded to 13% (INR201cr) from 11.5% in FY25 due to higher mix of credit (32-36% interest), insurance, and float income; OpEx efficiency improved via network optimization; credit loss rates stable due to platform-led underwriting

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Deep last-mile physical distribution: the agent network had grown to over 1.7 million agents across 2.6 lakh villages and 6,475 blocks as of March 2026, a footprint that is hard to replicate for assisted rural financial services.
- Trusted, daily touchpoints that give a structural advantage in serving rural customers whose service, trust and assistance needs differ materially from urban markets.
- Proprietary transaction data on agents' cash flows and behaviour, used to develop customised credit products and to convert field-level data into MSME credit signals.
- Distribution operating leverage: gross margin grew ~13% in FY26 while indirect costs did not grow, and EBIT expanded 2.4x, indicating fee-product rollout rides on an already-built cost base.
- Debt-free balance sheet - the MD&A states the Company is debt-free, with only cash credit facilities taken to manage treasury funds.
- Cross-sell traction: 23% of active Adhikaris now offer two or more financial products beyond basic cash withdrawal, evidencing the network can carry higher-margin categories.
- 365-day, seven-language customer support integrated with the partner web and mobile applications, supporting an agent base that needs assisted service.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Macro slowdown impacting rural discretionary spending; regulatory delays in BC-BO guidelines; UPI Cash Point adoption lag if major UPI app (1 remaining) delays integration; credit portfolio quality deterioration if repeat borrower defaults rise

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: UPI Cash Point is not a new license but a network play — DiGiSPICE’s 1.7M agents are the moat; agent lending is a self-reinforcing flywheel: more transactions → better data → better underwriting → higher loan ticket → more agent stickiness → more transactions; float income from 1.65M bank accounts (INR50L/quarter) is an underappreciated recurring revenue stream

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Mission framed as using technology to transform how Bharat banks, executed through three building blocks: expanding the network of Assisted Digital Touchpoint Operators (Spice Money Adhikaris) as a cost-efficient alternative to ATMs and bank branches; empowering that network to deliver a full suite of own and partner financial products; and creating digital products and apps for new-to-tech, under-banked consumers.
- Shift the growth thesis from adding touchpoints to deepening each touchpoint: management states the marginal contribution to business value from further network expansion will be …
